text: If a curve passes through the point (1, –2) and has slope of the tangent at any point (x, y) on it as $\frac{x^{2}-2y}{x}$, then the curve also passes through the point :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{x^{2}-2y}{x}$                    (Given)

$\frac{dy}{dx}+2\frac{y}{x}=x$

I.F = $e^{\int \frac{2}{x}dx}=x^{2}$

$\therefore$  $y.x^{2} =$ $\int x.x^{2}dx+C$

= $\frac{x^{4}}{y}+C$

This curve passes through (1, $-$ 2) $\Rightarrow$  C= $-$ $\frac{9}{4}$

$\therefore$  $yx^{2} =$ $\frac{x^{4}}{4}-\frac{9}{4}$

Now check option(s), Which is satisly by option (ii)

text:
If $\sin ^{4}α$ $+ 4 \cos ^{4}β$ + 2 = 4$\sqrt{2}$ sin $α$ cos $β$; $α$, $β$ $\in$ [0, $π$], 

then cos($α$ + $β$) $-$ cos($α$ $-$ $β$) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the non-negative numbers $\sin ^{4}α,4\cos ^{4}β,1,1$, A.M. $\geq$ G.M. gives

$\sin ^{4}α+4\cos ^{4}β+1+1\geq 4\left (4\sin ^{4}α\cos ^{4}β\right )^{1/4}=4\sqrt{2}|\sin α\cos β|\geq 4\sqrt{2}\sin α\cos β.$

The given equation says equality holds throughout, so the four numbers are equal, $\sin ^{4}α=4\cos ^{4}β=1$, and $\sin α\cos β\geq 0$.

Since $α\in [0,π]$, $\sin α\geq 0$, so $\sin α=1$, i.e. $α=\dfrac{π}{2}$.

$\cos ^{4}β=\dfrac{1}{4}\Rightarrow \cos β=\pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, and $\sin α\cos β\geq 0$ gives $\cos β=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, so $β=\dfrac{π}{4}$ and $\sin β=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

$\cos (α+β)-\cos (α-β)=-2\sin α\sin β=-2(1)\left (\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )=-\sqrt{2}.$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot

text: Let f be a differentiable function such that f(1) = 2 and f '(x) = f(x) for all x $\in$ R R. If h(x) = f(f(x)), then h'(1) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{f^{'}(x)}{f(x)}=1\forall x\in R$

Intergrate & use f(1) = 2

$f(x) = 2e^{x-1}$ $\Rightarrow$   $f '(x) = 2e^{x-1}$

h(x) = f(f(x)) $\Rightarrow$ h'(x) = f '(f(x))  f'(x)

h'(1) = f '(f(1)) f'(1)

= f '(2) f '(1)

= 2e . 2 = 4e
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot
